title: AutoMedBench: Medical AutoResearch with Agentic AI
hook: Can an AI agent run a whole medical-imaging research project end to end? AutoMedBench scores each stage — and finds agents can build pipelines but can't tell when they're broken.
key_points: A workflow-aware benchmark for autonomous medical-AI research, not just final-answer accuracy.
Organizes each run into five stages — Plan, Setup, Validate, Inference, Submit — across long-horizon tasks (~33 turns each).
Covers segmentation, image enhancement, VQA, report generation, and lesion detection at two difficulty tiers.
Validate is the weakest stage; verification and submission failures dominate errors, while task-understanding errors are rare (0.9%).
content_html: As AI agents are pushed toward running real research workflows rather than answering one-off questions, we need ways to evaluate the process, not just the final output. AutoMedBench does this for medical-AI research, where an agent must take a task brief and carry it all the way through to a submitted artifact.
extra_html:
How it works

Each task is decomposed into a unified five-stage workflow — Plan, Setup, Validate, Inference, and Submit (S1–S5) — and runs are long-horizon, averaging about 33 agent turns. The benchmark spans five research tracks: segmentation, image enhancement, visual question answering, report generation, and lesion detection, each at a "Lite" and a "Standard" tier that share data and metrics but differ in how much scaffolding the brief provides. Crucially, every run is scored both on final task performance and on per-stage scores, enabling stage-level diagnosis from brief to submission.

Why it matters

The stage-level view is what makes the findings interesting. Across thousands of runs, Validate is the weakest stage and Setup the strongest — current agents are better at making a pipeline executable than at checking whether it's reliable. Post-run analysis backs this up: verification and submission failures dominate tagged errors (37.7% and 38.1%), while task-understanding errors are rare at 0.9%. The lesson generalizes well beyond medicine: today's research agents tend to fail not because they misunderstand the goal, but because they don't verify their own work.

flashcards.prompt: What was AutoMedBench's headline finding about where research agents fail?

choices.text: Validate is the weakest stage — agents build pipelines but don't verify their own work
Agents most often misunderstand the task brief
Agents fail mainly at the initial planning stage

flashcards.explanation_html: Setup was strongest and Validate weakest; verification/submission failures dominated errors while task-understanding errors were rare (0.9%).

flashcards.prompt: What lesson does AutoMedBench say generalizes beyond medicine?

choices.text: Today's agents fail by not verifying their work, not by misunderstanding the goal
Longer task horizons always improve agent reliability
Medical tasks are uniquely too hard for agents

flashcards.explanation_html: The stage-level view shows verification, not comprehension, is the bottleneck — a lesson that applies to research agents broadly.
